title: Upper probability level
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $0<\epsilon<1/2$, and let $f$ be a monotone, nonconstant Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. The biased-minus probability polynomial of $f$ at the upper parameter corresponding to level $1-\epsilon$ equals $1-\epsilon$; that parameter is the unique one in $(0,1)$ where the polynomial has value $1-\epsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
